title: Research question first: why should WTI be tied to Brent?
rubric: States a testable hypothesis: WTI and Brent are tied by a long-run equilibrium (a stable discount) maintained by arbitrage; deviations close over days or weeks.
Names the mechanism: both are light sweet crudes; US exports, pipelines and shipping let traders buy the cheap one and sell the dear one — the discount reflects transport and logistics costs.

Predicts the statistical signature: daily returns strongly correlated, log levels moving together, the log spread fluctuating around a stable value (stationary) — and says that a high level correlation would NOT be evidence.
Selects variables with reasons: Brent as the main driver; Dubai as a related benchmark (likely redundant — same global factor); coffee as a control with no mechanism.

Anticipates what can break the link: export restrictions, Cushing storage or pipeline bottlenecks, regional supply shocks — and that the 2015 end of the export ban may have changed the relationship, so the sample choice must be tested.
Says which methods will test it and in which order: correlation and simple OLS on returns, ADF on each series, Engle-Granger and an ECM on levels, then a stability test around the known date.
